chapter: Favorite horn players and the Picou job
title: Big Eye Louis, Picou's job and Lewis Madison
summary: He worked with Big Eye Louis on Frenchmen Street and about five years with Picou at a place on Cleveland and Franklin, with Talbert, Glenny and Robichaux. He also liked Lewis Madison on second trumpet.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: And I played Tats. And I played with Louie Big Eye Louie.
I knew him. And I played with him quite a while.
Where did you work with him?
I worked with him in a little place but Dutchess on Frenchmen and Ferran.
Oh yes. That's before I got to hear him. Yeah. And I heard about the place.
Then I played with Pico for Dutchess on Cleveland and Frenchman. I played there about five years we played on that job.

With Elmer Talbot. They used to have, Cuckoo used to play the clarinet. And the cornet and Albert Glennie was our bass player. That was his job. Harry Robichaux, Harry Robichaux used to be the ghetto player.
Yeah I heard him years ago.
And then my other favorite trumpet player was Schatz, Lewis Madison.
Yeah I knew him. He was a good. Oh man.
I used to like to hear him play second trumpet. The record was good too.
Yeah I heard him on bass. I did hear him in a parade once on trumpet too. He played alto, what's in his house for us. Yeah.
